about: Chapter 10, Symmetrical Designs: 69 patterns, three or four for each of the 15 skills (1 and 2 marks), three 3-mark and three 5-mark written questions, and three 4-mark case studies, drawn from the chapter's 500 questions. Only what words alone state fully is generated: grid rows as X and dots, points as (across, up), named shapes, plain capital letters and a stated digit code. All DRAFT until Ashalatha approves them.

patterns.text: A {d} has {p} pairs of matching points on opposite sides of its mirror line, and {q} more {'point lies' if q == 1 else 'points lie'} on the mirror line itself. How many points are there altogether?
patterns.hint: Each pair has two points. A point on the mirror line is its own partner.
patterns.explanation: {p} pairs give 2 × {p} = {2 * p} points. Adding the {q} on the line gives {2 * p + q}.
patterns.misconception: Treats equal area or similar-looking parts as mirror images without checking point-to-point matching.
patterns.notes: 2 to 12 pairs, 1 to 5 points on the line.

choice.w2: Yes, if the line is straight

patterns.text: A {f} is {r.d} squares to the {r.s} of a vertical mirror line on a grid. Where is its image?

wrong.mistake: keeps the image on the same side
counts the line itself as a square
doubles the distance from the line

patterns.hint: The image is the same distance from the line, on the other side.
patterns.explanation: A vertical mirror swaps left and right but keeps the distance: {r.d} squares to the {r.o}.
patterns.misconception: Copies a half without reversing its left–right orientation or places points at unequal distances from the axis.
patterns.notes: 2 to 9 squares, left or right of the line.

patterns.text: In a grid row, X is a coloured cell and . is an empty cell. The left half, read from the outer edge towards a vertical mirror, is “{h.s}”. Write the right half, read from the mirror towards the outer edge.
patterns.hint: The cell next to the mirror on the left matches the cell next to the mirror on the right.
patterns.explanation: Read the left half backwards, starting at the mirror: “{h.r}”.
patterns.misconception: Copies a half without reversing its left–right orientation or places points at unequal distances from the axis.
patterns.notes: Halves of 3 to 5 cells that are not the same backwards (so copying is wrong). Answer: X and dots.

patterns.text: A {d} has a vertical mirror line. {k} marked {'point lies' if k == 1 else 'points lie'} on the line and {m} marked points lie to its left. The design is completed by reflecting. How many marked points does the whole design have?
patterns.hint: Points on the line do not move. Each point on the left gets a partner on the right.
patterns.explanation: The {m} points on the left get {m} partners, and the {k} on the line stay: {k} + 2 × {m} = {k + 2 * m}.
patterns.misconception: Copies a half without reversing its left–right orientation or places points at unequal distances from the axis.
patterns.notes: 1 to 6 points on the line, 2 to 12 to its left.

patterns.text: On a grid, the columns are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on from the left. A vertical mirror line runs down the middle of column {c}. A dot is in column {x}. Which column is its image in, and how many columns apart are the dot and its image? Give the column first.

steps.text: The dot is {c - x} {'column' if (c - x) == 1 else 'columns'} left of column {c}, so its image is in column {c} + {c - x} = {2 * c - x}.
They are {2 * c - x} − {x} = {2 * (c - x)} {'column' if (2 * (c - x)) == 1 else 'columns'} apart.

patterns.hint: Count how far the dot is from the mirror column, then go the same distance on the other side.
patterns.explanation: Column {x} is {c - x} left of column {c}; the image is {c - x} right of it, in column {2 * c - x}, {2 * (c - x)} {'column' if (2 * (c - x)) == 1 else 'columns'} away.
patterns.misconception: Copies a half without reversing its left–right orientation or places points at unequal distances from the axis.
patterns.notes: Mirror column 6 to 12, dot to its left; images within 20 columns.

patterns.responseFormat: Two rows separated by a semicolon
patterns.text: In a grid, X is a coloured cell and . is an empty cell. Just above a horizontal mirror line is the row “{p.a}”, and above that is the row “{p.b}”. Write the row just below the mirror line, then the row below that.

steps.text: The row just below the line matches the row just above it: “{p.a}”.
The next row down matches the next row up: “{p.b}”.

patterns.hint: A horizontal mirror does not change left and right. It changes the order of the rows.
patterns.explanation: Rows reflect in reverse order across the line, each row unchanged: “{p.a}”, then “{p.b}”.
patterns.misconception: Moves a feature sideways or keeps it on the same side instead of reflecting across the horizontal line.
patterns.notes: Rows of 3 or 4 cells; the two rows differ.

patterns.text: {who.name} draws a star {a} {'row' if a == 1 else 'rows'} above a horizontal mirror line, and its copy {a + e} rows below the line. How many rows too far from the line is the copy?
patterns.hint: The copy should be as far below the line as the star is above it.
patterns.explanation: The copy should be {a} {'row' if a == 1 else 'rows'} below. It is {a + e} − {a} = {e} too far.
patterns.misconception: Moves a feature sideways or keeps it on the same side instead of reflecting across the horizontal line.
patterns.notes: Star 1 to 7 rows above; copy 1 to 5 rows too far.

patterns.text: On a grid, the rows are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on from the top. A horizontal mirror line runs along the middle of row {r}. A cell in row {y} is coloured. Which row is its image in, and how many rows apart are the cell and its image? Give the row first.

steps.text: Row {y} is {r - y} {'row' if (r - y) == 1 else 'rows'} above row {r}, so the image is in row {r} + {r - y} = {2 * r - y}.
They are {2 * r - y} − {y} = {2 * (r - y)} {'row' if (2 * (r - y)) == 1 else 'rows'} apart.

patterns.hint: Count how far the cell is from the mirror row, then go the same distance below it.
patterns.explanation: Row {y} is {r - y} above row {r}; the image is {r - y} below it, in row {2 * r - y}.
patterns.misconception: Moves a feature sideways or keeps it on the same side instead of reflecting across the horizontal line.
patterns.notes: Mirror row 6 to 12, cell above it; images within 20 rows.

patterns.text: Points on a grid are written (across, up). Reflect the point ({a}, {b}) in the diagonal line through (0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2) and so on. Give the across number of the image first, then the up number.
patterns.hint: Reflecting in this diagonal swaps the two numbers.
patterns.explanation: The image of ({a}, {b}) is ({b}, {a}).
patterns.misconception: Treats diagonal reflection as a quarter turn or changes only one coordinate without following the mirror rule.
patterns.notes: Points with both numbers 0 to 12, never on the line.

patterns.text: Points on a grid are written (across, up). Which point stays in the same place when it is reflected in the diagonal line through (0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2) and so on?

wrong.mistake: thinks any point near the line stays fixed
thinks a point with its numbers swapped stays fixed
thinks nearly equal numbers are enough

patterns.hint: A point stays fixed only if it is on the mirror line.
patterns.explanation: Points on the line have equal numbers, like {f.c}, so they do not move.
patterns.misconception: Treats diagonal reflection as a quarter turn or changes only one coordinate without following the mirror rule.
patterns.notes: The fixed point has equal numbers 1 to 9; the others do not.

patterns.text: Points on a grid are written (across, up). A learner reflects ({e.a}, {e.b}) in the diagonal line through (0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2) and so on, and writes ({e.a}, {e.a}). What should the image be?

wrong.mistake: changes only one number
leaves the point where it is
copies one number into both places

patterns.hint: Reflecting in this diagonal swaps the across and up numbers.
patterns.explanation: Swap the numbers: ({e.a}, {e.b}) becomes {e.c}.
patterns.misconception: Treats diagonal reflection as a quarter turn or changes only one coordinate without following the mirror rule.
patterns.notes: Points with different numbers 1 to 9.

patterns.text: Points on a grid are written (across, up). A triangle has corners A({t.a}, {t.b}), B({t.c}, {t.d}) and C({t.k}, {t.k}). It is reflected in the diagonal line through (0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2) and so on. How many corners move? What is the image of A? Give the number of corners, then the across and up numbers of A's image.

steps.text: C is on the line, so it stays; A and B move: 2 corners.
A's image: swap the numbers to get ({t.b}, {t.a}).

patterns.hint: A point on the mirror line has equal numbers and does not move.
patterns.explanation: C({t.k}, {t.k}) is on the line. A and B have different numbers, so they move. A goes to ({t.b}, {t.a}).
patterns.misconception: Treats diagonal reflection as a quarter turn or changes only one coordinate without following the mirror rule.
patterns.notes: A and B off the line, C on it; numbers 0 to 11.

patterns.text: The outline of {o} is a {s.c}: all {s.n} sides are equal and all its angles are equal. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
patterns.hint: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides.
patterns.explanation: A regular polygon with {s.n} sides has {s.n} lines of symmetry.
patterns.misconception: Counts every diagonal as a symmetry line or assumes all shapes with equal sides have the same number of lines.
patterns.notes: Regular pentagon to regular 12-sided shape (the square and triangle are in S05-P2).

patterns.stimulus: Case study: Points on a grid are written (across, up). {who.name} plans a rangoli on a grid with a vertical centre line where every point has across number {l.a}. A lamp is placed at ({l.x}, {l.y}).

parts.text: (a) What is the across number of the lamp's mirror image?
parts.explanation: {l.a - l.x} before {l.a}, so {l.a - l.x} past it: {l.i}.

parts.text: (b) What is the up number of the mirror image?
parts.explanation: A vertical mirror does not change the up number: {l.y}.

parts.text: (c) How many squares apart are the lamp and its image?
(d) Which of these lamp positions does not move when reflected?
